cpu_binding.digit: Original all-worker-thread CPU2 binding after imports

timing: Sum of the three original synchronized 100-batch windows, excluding initialization, warmup and between-window records
primary_statistic: Maximum of five same-round ratios: GIDS complete 300-batch time / DiGiT complete 300-batch time. Select on raw precision; earliest round wins an exact tie.
retain: Selected round and both run identities
Existing host stages and I/O counters
monitoring: one GPU admission per fresh worker; window-boundary counters and progress; no continuous monitor
limits: The displayed result is the maximum observed paired speedup out of five rounds, not a typical, mean or interference-free speedup.
Both selected times come from the same round. Never combine the slowest GIDS from one round with the fastest DiGiT from another.
This selection rule differs from the previous ratio of per-system minima; preserve the old three-run result separately.
Five fixed rounds, ten fresh processes: G-D / D-G / G-D / D-G / G-D. Retain all rounds, including slow or negative results, without retries.
GIDS retains default CPU scheduling; DiGiT retains original CPU2 binding. The system comparison includes this difference.
A failed or incomplete round stops the series with preserved partial evidence; do not select from fewer than five complete rounds.
Every worker uses 20 warmup plus 300 measured batches. No accuracy, full epoch, long-term stability or causal claim.
UKS uses synthetic features/labels and accepted ABI4 backend; only the IG bounded-window and selection/affinity protocol are reused. No continuous IG telemetry instrumentation.
